questions.knowledge_point: Using the Double-Angle Formula Multiple Times
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's recall the double-angle formula for sine: 

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x=\operatorname{sin}⁡2x
$$

Substituting $x={7.5}^{∘}$ into the above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{sin}⁡({7.5}^{∘})\operatorname{cos}⁡({7.5}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot {7.5}^{∘})\end{aligned}
$$

which simplifies as

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{sin}⁡({7.5}^{∘})\operatorname{cos}⁡({7.5}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡({15}^{∘}).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can rewrite the given expression using the above, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}4\operatorname{sin}⁡({7.5}^{∘})\operatorname{cos}⁡({7.5}^{∘})\operatorname{cos}⁡({15}^{∘}) & =2\cdot 2\operatorname{sin}⁡({7.5}^{∘})\operatorname{cos}⁡({7.5}^{∘})\operatorname{cos}⁡({15}^{∘}) \\  & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡({15}^{∘})\operatorname{cos}⁡({15}^{∘})\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the double-angle formula once more with $x={15}^{∘},$ we can further simplify the above expression: 

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡{15}^{∘}\operatorname{cos}⁡{15}^{∘}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot {15}^{∘})=\operatorname{sin}⁡({30}^{∘})
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}4\operatorname{sin}⁡({7.5}^{∘})\operatorname{cos}⁡({7.5}^{∘})\operatorname{cos}⁡({15}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡({30}^{∘})=\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Using the Double-Angle Formula to Simplify Ratios
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's recall the double-angle formula for sine: 

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡2x=2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x
$$

Substituting $x=\frac{\pi }{12}$ into the above, we get

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{12})=2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})
$$

which simplifies as

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})=2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12}).
$$

Therefore, we can simplify the given expression by rewriting the $\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})$ in the numerator, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})}{{cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})} & =\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})}{{cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})} \\  & =\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})}}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})}} \\  & =\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})} \\  & =2\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12}).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Using the Double-Angle Formula to Simplify Ratios
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's recall the double-angle formula for sine: 

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡2x=2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x
$$

Substituting $x=\frac{\pi }{16}$ into the above, we get

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{16})=2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{16})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{16})
$$

which simplifies as

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8})=2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{16})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{16}).
$$

Therefore, we can simplify the given expression by rewriting the $\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8})$ in the numerator, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8})}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{16})} & =\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{16})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{16})}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{16})} \\  & =\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{16})\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{16})}}{\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{16})}} \\  & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{16}).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding Exact Value of a Trigonometric Expression Using the Double-Angle Formula
questions.worked_solution:
First, we note that:

$$
\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8})}{\operatorname{sec}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8})}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8})\cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{sec}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8})}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8})
$$

Now, let's recall the double-angle formula for sine: 

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x=\operatorname{sin}⁡2x
$$

Substituting $x=\frac{\pi }{8}$ into the above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{8}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we obtain

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8})=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8})}{\operatorname{sec}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8})}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding Exact Value of a Trigonometric Expression Using the Double-Angle Formula
questions.worked_solution:
Let's recall the double-angle formula for sine:

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)
$$

Substituting $x={15}^{∘}$ into the above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{sin}⁡({15}^{∘})\operatorname{cos}⁡({15}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot {15}^{∘}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡({30}^{∘}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}4\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡({15}^{∘})\operatorname{cos}⁡({15}^{∘}) & =2\sqrt{3}\cdot 2\operatorname{sin}⁡({15}^{∘})\operatorname{cos}⁡({15}^{∘}) \\  & =2\sqrt{3}\cdot (\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
